divergesFromReason: Angular delegates Toast to Angular Material's MatSnackBar (frameworks/angular/behaviour-delegated.json), which has no tone axis at all -- so its binding stays the flat pattern "alert" it always was, while React's varies role and aria-live by tone and is cased. What MatSnackBar actually renders, read against the installed @angular/material 22.0.5 in node_modules/@angular/material/fesm2022/snack-bar.mjs: MatSnackBarConfig.politeness defaults to 'polite', the container resolves _live to 'assertive' only when politeness === 'assertive' && !announcementMessage, and _role is assigned ONLY inside `if (this._platform.FIREFOX)`. The template binds [attr.aria-live]="_live" [attr.role]="_role", so outside Firefox a snackbar carries aria-live="polite" and NO ROLE, whatever the message says. This divergence therefore has a cost to a real person rather than being merely structural: a critical error toast interrupts in React (role="alert", aria-live="assertive") and is queued in Angular. It is recorded and DEFERRED TO PLAN D -- a decision rather than a resolution, and nothing is fixed for an Angular user until Plan D lands -- in components-divergences.md's "Toast -- a critical error interrupts in React and is queued in Angular". HISTORY, because this clause used to claim otherwise: until 8C10 it read "the same treatment Skeleton's divergence got", and that stopped being true when Skeleton's divergence was closed and its entry RETIRED. The two are now contrasting cases rather than matching ones -- Skeleton's closed because one layer was simply wrong and the definition of what a skeleton is for settled it, while this one is deferred precisely because neither layer is wrong: Angular delegates to a control that has no tone axis to be wrong about, so there is nothing to fix at this layer's level and Plan D is where an arena-toast on the CDK would carry the role per tone. Note what this reason does NOT claim: behaviour-delegated.json's Toast entry binds `alert` with no exceptions while MatSnackBar renders no role, so that entry is inaccurate. It is left untouched on purpose -- that inaccuracy is pre-existing and belongs to CLAUDE.md's standing "every claim the delegated declarations make about Angular Material is unpinned" entry, and this binding must not stack a fresh claim on top of it.

exceptions.reason: Toast.jsx has no timer of its own, but its doc comment describes toasts as auto-dismissed by the host by default and `persist` as the opt-out. Nothing in this file enforces persist for a critical state, so the claim rests on the host.

cases.name: advisory
cases.when: any other tone -- role="status" with aria-live="polite"
